scaleDegrees: Minor 3rd (Mediant) - Characteristic tone defining minor quality
Major 7th (Leading Tone) - Raised from natural minor, smooth resolution
theory.mode: Not a mode of major scale - independent scale family. Minor scale with raised 6th and 7th. Creates smooth leading tone. Parent scale of many jazz modes (Altered scale = 7th mode, Lydian Dominant = 4th mode, Lydian Augmented = 3rd mode)

practiceExercises.name: A Melodic Minor Scale Runs
practiceExercises.description: Practice the A melodic minor scale ascending and descending, focusing on the raised 6th and 7th that distinguish it from natural minor
instructions: Start slowly with metronome at 60 BPM, playing A melodic minor ascending and descending
Compare with A natural minor to hear the raised F# and G# that define the jazz melodic minor sound
Practice in multiple positions across the fretboard to build familiarity in all registers

practiceExercises.name: Melodic Minor Modal Exploration
practiceExercises.description: Play the melodic minor scale starting from each degree to hear its important modes: Lydian Dominant (4th degree), Mixolydian ♭6 (5th degree), and Altered (7th degree)
instructions: Play A melodic minor starting from D to hear Lydian Dominant, then from E for Mixolydian ♭6
Play from G# to hear the Altered scale (Super Locrian), the most important jazz mode of melodic minor
Apply each mode over its corresponding chord type: Lydian Dominant over dom7#11, Altered over V7alt

practiceExercises.name: Jazz Minor ii-V-i Application
practiceExercises.description: Apply melodic minor harmony to a jazz minor ii-V-i progression, using appropriate modes over each chord
instructions: Play over F#m7♭5 - E7alt - Am(maj7) using Locrian #2, Altered scale, and melodic minor respectively
Focus on smooth voice leading between chords, letting guide tones connect the changes
Record yourself and listen back, checking that your lines clearly outline the harmony

relatedScales.differences: Melodic minor raises both the 6th and 7th degrees, eliminating the augmented 2nd gap found in harmonic minor
relatedScales.usage: Darker, simpler minor sound; melodic minor adds sophistication with the raised 6th and 7th

relatedScales.differences: Harmonic minor raises only the 7th; melodic minor raises both 6th and 7th, creating smoother melodic motion
relatedScales.usage: Harmonic minor has the exotic augmented 2nd interval; melodic minor smooths this out for jazz contexts

relatedScales.differences: Dorian has ♭7 while melodic minor has natural 7th; both feature the characteristic natural 6th in a minor context
relatedScales.usage: Dorian is simpler and more common for minor 7th chords; melodic minor adds the leading tone for minor-major 7th chords
